# TASSEL

## Role

TASSEL (Trait Analysis by aSSociation, Evolution and Linkage) is a widely used
plant-genetics application and command-line pipeline for genotype/phenotype
association, linkage disequilibrium, diversity, kinship, PCA, and genomic
selection. Its modern documentation supports common genotype formats including
HapMap, VCF, PLINK, FASTA, and HDF5, plus GLM and MLM association workflows.

## simitall Position

TASSEL is the preferred external association-analysis suggestion for plant
studies when the user requests plant-standard TASSEL output, HapMap/GBS-oriented
processing, LD/kinship/PCA inspection, or an explicit TASSEL comparison. The
R-native `analyze_gwas()` path remains the portable default when an all-R
workflow is requested.

## Inputs

- Genotype data in a supported format and a marker map/reference coordinate system.
- Trait, covariate, and population/family metadata with exact taxa-name matching.
- Prespecified filtering, kinship/structure choices, and association model.

## Outputs and Validation

- Filtered genotype/trait inputs, kinship and PCA/structure summaries,
  association results, Manhattan/QQ plots, and a method manifest.
- In synthetic data, evaluate TASSEL results with the same causal truth and
  recovery window used for the R baseline or other methods.

## Guardrails

- TASSEL is common in crop genetics, especially maize, but it is not a
  scientifically mandatory default for every plant study.
- Taxa-name mismatches, genotype encoding, missingness, and structure decisions
  can change results before any association model is fitted.
- Do not compare methods unless input filtering and covariates are harmonized.

## Tutorial Provenance

Curated from user-supplied `Tassel_User_Guide_3.0.pdf` and the current TASSEL
user documentation. The supplied guide is TASSEL 3; use current TASSEL 5
manuals for present-day commands and file support.
